text: “Each message block, M^(1), M^(2), …, M^(N), is processed in order, using the following steps:”
notes: Printed p. 22; PDF p. 27. [extraction repaired] Superscripts restored. Sequential processing is exercised by the two-block and nine-block sequences; tc2_block1 checks the first intermediate result.

text: “The top level entity is called sha256_core. This entity has wide interfaces (512 bit block input, 256 bit digest).”
notes: The checked interface is the core itself. No wrapper behavior is claimed.

text: “Note that the core does NOT implement padding of final block. The caller is expected to handle padding.”
notes: The supplied testbench provides prepared 512-bit blocks (lines 385-393 and 480-492). FIPS 180-4 section 6.2.1 describes preprocessing; no padding engine is claimed for this interface.

text: A new message is started with init and a supplied block; later blocks are started with next after ready. The double-block and nine-block tasks deassert each request after one clock period. The single-block task leaves init asserted through its ready wait and digest comparison.
notes: Bench lines 262-268, 307-321, 399-453. Simultaneous init and next, requests during processing, and arbitrary request pulse lengths are outside the exercised sequence.

text: The testbench waits while ready is low, then reads the digest or submits the next block. In the original RTL, ready is asserted in the idle state; processing completes with the digest update before returning to that state.
notes: Bench wait_ready polls ready every clock period; it does not impose an exact latency or independently check every ready transition.

text: The original RTL clears digest_valid on an init or next request accepted in the idle state and asserts it when the block digest is updated. The testbench connects and displays digest_valid, but its wait and digest comparisons use ready and digest; it does not assert digest_valid.
notes: No checkpoint independently verifies digest_valid. An empty checkpoint list deliberately distinguishes this observed RTL behavior from checked handshake behavior.

text: The testbench sets mode to 1 at initialization and leaves it at 1 for all supplied sequences. This selects the SHA-256 initial words in the core; SHA-224 mode and mode changes during processing are not checked.
notes: Bench line 206 is the only mode assignment. Full combinational blocks are mapped without claiming the alternate mode is exercised.

text: The double-block task compares the first intermediate digest at tc2_block1 and the chained second-block digest at tc2_block2. The nine-block sequence starts once with init, continues eight times with next, and compares only the final digest at issue9.
notes: All preceding blocks contribute to each chained result. The nine-block task does not compare its intermediate digests. The standard defines ordered block processing; these checkpoint and interface details come from the bench.

text: Before the digest tests, the testbench drives reset_n low for four half-clock periods and releases it. The original core then accepts the initial request from its idle state. Reset during an active block and individual register reset values are not independently compared.
notes: The mapped sequential blocks include reset and ordinary register updates. Reachability of the checked sequence depends on initialization; equality of every reset value is not established.
